newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil sees earlier start up of Vigdis oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Statoil sees earlier start up of Vigdis oilfield.

text.p: Saga Petroleum's Vigdis oilfield in the North Sea may come onstream in late February, a month ahead of schedule, Den Norske Stats Oljeselskap ASA's (Statoil) Status Weekly newsletter said on Thursday.
A spokesman for operator Saga said he could not confirm Statoil's report.
"We are working to get Vigdis onstream as soon as possible but I cannot confirm any date," the spokesman said.
In May, Saga brought forward start up of Vigdis to April 1, 1997 from the original scheduled of July 1. Later the company announced cost savings of 400 million crowns in the 5.1 billion crown budget.
The field is being developed via seabed installation tied-back to the Snorre platform where oil will be processed.
Stabilised crude will be transferred via dedicated pipeline to Gullfaks A for storage and offshore loading into shuttle tankers.

Vigdis output is expected to plateau at 95,000 barrels per day (bpd) over three years. Field life is forecast at 15 years. Estimated recoverable reserves are put at 24.9 million cubic metres of oil (185 million barrels) of oil and two billion cubic metres of natural gas.

Saga as operator holds a 7.7 percent stake in Vigdis and is partnered by Statoil with 55.4 percent, Esso with 10.5 percent, Idemitsu with 9.6 percent, Norsk Hydro with 8.4 percent, Elf with 5.6 percent and Deminex with 2.8 percent.
